title: Environmentally Relevant Lambda‐Cyhalothrin Concentration Induces Genotoxicity and Oxidative Stress in the Early Life Stages of Rhinella arenarum
content:
ABSTRACT

Pyrethroid insecticides are frequently reported in aquatic environments as a consequence of their extensive use in agricultural and domestic applications. However, their impact on non-target organisms, particularly amphibians, remains poorly understood. In this investigation, we studied DNA damage and oxidative stress-related responses in Rhinella arenarum tadpoles exposed to an environmentally relevant concentration of lambda-cyhalothrin (LCT). Laboratory acute exposure was performed at 0.1 μg/L of LCT, employing Karate with Zeon Technology (25% LCT). Experiments were conducted after 48 and 96 h of treatment. The alkaline comet assay was used to examine DNA integrity by detecting strand breaks involving both single- and double-stranded DNA. Oxidative status was characterised through catalase (CAT) and glutathione S-transferase (GST) activities, together with reduced glutathione (GSH) content. The data revealed that LCT exposure increased DNA strand breaks by 4.1- and 4.8-fold at 48 and 96 h, respectively. At 48 h, CAT and GST activities increased, whereas GSH content decreased, suggesting an early antioxidant response accompanied by glutathione depletion. In contrast, after 96 h, CAT and GSH levels increased, while GST activity remained unchanged. Our findings highlight the importance of employing the comet assay together with the estimation of antioxidant responses for the early detection of environmental toxicity in amphibian monitoring programmes, particularly for assessing pesticide exposure. Taken together, these results improve the current understanding of the ecological risk that the pyrethroid LCT poses to aquatic environments.
